recorded_queries: robot VLA partial instruction revision constraint preservation task switching 2025 2026
topic_groups: image-text interleaved instructions and visual references
search.authority: Official proceedings and conference listings for publication; author arXiv versions for stated sections. Secondary summaries used only for discovery.
search.stop_rule: Three candidate questions compared; closest works, strong simple baseline, and next discriminating non-experimental action specified.
access_notes: OpenReview Interleave forum presented access challenge; official ICLR listing used for venue and arXiv v2 for content. No bypass.
Interleave HTML v3 and IVA HTML v2 were unavailable; use explicitly identified older versions. No assumption that these equal final proceedings.
Do What quantitative values were not used because the viewed versions were not reconciled.

sources.title: Yell At Your Robot: Improving On-the-Fly from Language Corrections
sources.use: Language feedback for hierarchical robot control is prior work.
sources.boundary: Full text and code not audited in this scout.

sources.title: Hi Robot: Open-Ended Instruction Following with Hierarchical Vision-Language-Action Models
sources.use: Feedback, negative constraints, situated corrections and high-level oracle already exist.
sources.boundary: Selected arXiv v1 sections; no claim of complete review or version equality with final proceedings. Public native interface not yet audited.

sources.title: SwitchVLA: Execution-Aware Task Switching for Vision-Language-Action Models
sources.use: Execution-conditioned switching and phase-specific pairwise/sequence evaluation are prior work.
sources.boundary: No new accepted-venue claim or native reproduction.

sources.title: ReSteer: Quantifying and Refining the Steerability of Multitask Robot Policies
sources.use: State-conditioned competence, steerability and task-success evaluation are existing formulations.
sources.boundary: A conjunction of constraints can already be represented by task success; no new metric/theory claim. Code URL is not evidence of implemented case support.

sources.title: Do VLAs Really Follow Instructions? Diagnosing How-Level Instruction Following in Vision-Language-Action Models
sources.use: Correction/retry/inverted controls, online guidance and instruction-only task conditions already studied.
sources.boundary: No full code/evaluator audit; not evidence that selective revision has never been studied elsewhere.

sources.title: Causeway: Restoring Task Accessibility for Instruction Switching in VLA Policies
sources.use: Prior-task state and target-task accessibility are competing explanations for switching failure.
sources.boundary: Method details and any exact comparison with retained constraints unverified; no quantitative result imported.

sources.title: Interleave-VLA: Enhancing Robot Manipulation with Image-Text Interleaved Instructions
sources.content_title: Interleave-VLA: Enhancing Robot Manipulation with Interleaved Image-Text Instructions
sources.use: Interleaved, goal-image and multiple-image instruction formats already supported.
sources.boundary: Final title from official listing differs slightly from preprint title. No claim that conflict is absent from every evaluation. Code README only, no implementation audit.

sources.title: Bring My Cup! Personalizing Vision-Language-Action Models with Visual Attentive Prompting
sources.use: Reference-image personalization of object selection is prior work.
sources.boundary: Not a full-text assessment of conflicting instructions or code reproducibility.

sources.title: Do What? Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models to Reject the Impossible
sources.use: False-premise detection/rejection is prior work; observability versus absence remains a provisional adjacent question.
sources.boundary: Not EMNLP main; older arXiv content and final abstract kept distinct. No quantitative synthesis or proof of absent occlusion evaluation.

claims.research_value: Worth a bounded exploratory comparison; a simple automatic restatement is the primary alternative.
